experiments.detail: The only model family represented at this rung. On the 31 GB machine the training matrix measured 14.9 GB under LightGBM and 33.5 GB under scikit-learn, so only LightGBM completed. That is a memory measurement, not a quality comparison: the other families were not run to completion here, and nothing about their detection performance follows from it.

release.scope_note: These counts describe the current main tree, which is where the website is deployed from. v0.2.1 remains the latest signed software release; it collected fewer tests, because the website's own tests were added after it. Result-artifact links below are pinned to v0.2.1, and every linked artifact was verified byte-identical between v0.2.1 and current main.

scale.note: the size of the largest corpus the evaluation protocol was carried to, published in the HI-Large report

stories.cannot: A preregistered sensitivity analysis on HI-Small, not evidence of leakage: part of the move comes from the naive split's higher prevalence, and nothing here claims the effect holds on another dataset.
stories.lede: Two temporal protocols on HI-Small, same cut date, 5 seeds each. The naive one readmits 966 positive transactions whose rings were already seen in training. Average precision then reads 40.0% higher, recall at a 50-alert budget 4.1% lower.
stories.shows: Both protocols on each metric's own scale; the two metrics move in opposite directions.
stories.title: Change how the test set is drawn and the metrics disagree

stories.cannot: The band is a property of the SPLIT, not of any model, so it does not transfer to another window, another rung or a production portfolio. The logistic level shown here is a withdrawn figure that the registry permits only in this qualified form: beside its null.
stories.lede: On the evaluated HI-Medium split a uniformly random ranker already attains precision@50 of 0.45392-0.49147 pooled, because the window has 12 thin days from 2022-09-17 on which almost every account-day is a positive. A level quoted without that band is unreadable.
stories.shows: Each observed precision@k next to the random-ranker band for the same budget on the same split. The gap, not the level, is the result.
stories.title: The same ranker is strong or ordinary depending on the day it is scored on

window.estimand: the precision@k a UNIFORMLY RANDOM ranker attains on the evaluated ring-aware test split -- the slot-weighted mean of daily account-day prevalence, bracketed because a truncated day bounds its population rather than fixing it. It is a property of the SPLIT, not of any model.

stories.cannot: Eight seeds bound what was observed rather than estimate a distribution, so the range is not a confidence interval.
stories.lede: 8 seeds of one GBDT configuration on HI-Medium, changing nothing but the seed. precision@50 runs 0.59144 to 0.89815, a span worth 37.19% of the mean.
stories.shows: Every seed as its own point, with the mean and the full observed range. A single-seed headline could have landed anywhere in this span.
stories.title: One seed is not a result: precision@50 spans 37.19% of its own mean

stories.cannot: Not a comparison of learners: scikit-learn gradient boosting needed a 33.5 GB training matrix against LightGBM's 14.9 GB on the roughly 31 GB machine and did not complete, which is a memory measurement and says nothing about how either learner would have scored.
stories.lede: The top rung of AMLworld is 179,702,229 transactions. The evaluation ran there on one 31 GB machine, three seeds, at a fixed training row order, under the same units, budgets and publication gate as the smaller rungs.
stories.shows: recall@200 for each HI-Large seed, linked to its manifest.
stories.title: The same protocol ran at 179.7M transactions

entries.now: withdrawn. Against the repository's own within-day permutation null the observed spread of 3.46875 sits at the 53.5th percentile of chance (p = 0.46633), and the per-typology ordering INVERTS: GATHER-SCATTER 0.9159, CYCLE 1.264, rho(rate, lift) = 0.3095
entries.was: the FIRST cliff-aware replacement for the typology-spread p-value: exposure 0.1925 (BIPARTITE) to 0.5863 (GATHER-SCATTER), rho 0.762 against detection, and p = 0.11-0.44 from assumed thin-day rates of 0.80/0.90/0.95
entries.why: two independent defects. (1) WRONG POPULATION: exposure was measured over every ring in the patterns file, including the 736 the ring-aware split drops, so it described a different ring set from the detection rates it was explaining. (2) INFEASIBLE ASSUMED RATES: an after-cliff share of 0.66352 and a pooled rate of 0.3724 cap the after-cliff rate at 0.56125, so 0.80/0.90/0.95 cannot reproduce the observed pooled rate at any head rate in [0,1]. Inside the feasible range the p-value spans 0.0014 to 0.9014, so the assumption chose the answer. Superseded entirely: the defensible null is the within-day permutation, not any binomial

entries.now: withdrawn. Against the repository's own within-day permutation null the observed spread of 3.46875 sits at the 53.5th percentile of chance (p = 0.46633), and the per-typology ordering INVERTS: GATHER-SCATTER 0.9159, CYCLE 1.264, rho(rate, lift) = 0.3095; exposure still correlates with the RAW rate at rho = 0.7857, exact permutation p = 0.02793, but that is a statement about the generator, not a detection result
entries.was: the SECOND cliff-aware replacement: exposure-only p = 0.0026 from fixed head/tail strata measured at ring budget 200 (tail 0.78348, head 0.57303, observed spread 1.85128, exposure-blind 1.2577), with rho 0.7143 and a t-approximated p = 0.0465
entries.why: three defects at once. (1) WRONG BUDGET: the 3.05x spread is ring_recall@50 -- src/aml/eval/metrics.py sets b = 50 -- while these strata were measured at 200, so the artifact published a tail rate of 0.78348 beside its own feasibility cap of 0.56125. (2) WRONG MODEL: medium_gbdt_s0 is source_lineage 'models'; its ring_recall@200 of 0.71267 matches none of the eight typology seeds. (3) WRONG NULL: two strata flatten a per-day process, and no binomial belongs on a budget-constrained metric. The rho was also a t-approximation on n=8; exactly, it is 0.0576, not 0.0465
